raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"From Bowling Green Park, carry on to Fraunces Tavern, about an 8-minute walk away.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Here's the first surprise — the tavern in front of you isn't quite the one Washington knew.","source_id":"349ecf1c-11df-43c6-979b-4a78ec332ca3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"How much of it is genuinely old is a matter of dispute: one account calls it a conjectural rebuild the Sons of the Revolution financed in 1907, with only a handful of original bricks left, while another dates the original.","source_id":"349ecf1c-11df-43c6-979b-4a78ec332ca3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["f781f822-038c-4e67-b8e6-c574371be401"]},{"text":"The style is Georgian, named for those British kings — though the new, antiroyalist states were quick to rebrand it \"colonial\" or \"federal.\"","source_id":"f781f822-038c-4e67-b8e6-c574371be401","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Long before any revolution, this was a private mansion — a wedding present that Colonel Stephanus Van Cortlandt, the city's tenth mayor, handed to his son-in-law Stephen Delancey, the French immigrant whose name still hangs on Delancey Street.","source_id":"89b55a2d-dcc0-4df7-b043-71871da49f1d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The tavern that made the place famous was run by Samuel Fraunces, an immigrant from the West Indies who'd go on to become Washington's steward.","source_id":"89b55a2d-dcc0-4df7-b043-71871da49f1d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["f765ed0c-2fc7-4d3a-ba8c-6c05b9815c58"]},{"text":"It's where the Committee of Correspondence — the body that became the Continental Congress — held its very first meeting, and where the Sons of Liberty gathered dozens of times to plot how to throw the British out.","source_id":"89b55a2d-dcc0-4df7-b043-71871da49f1d","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2,"also_cites":["349ecf1c-11df-43c6-979b-4a78ec332ca3"]},{"text":"When the war was won, Washington came back here to say goodbye to his officers in his famous Farewell to the Troops, and Alexander Hamilton set up his first Office of the Treasury under this roof.","source_id":"349ecf1c-11df-43c6-979b-4a78ec332ca3","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"Look east along Pearl Street and you'll catch one of the last block-long runs of late-1700s and early-1800s shipping offices and warehouses in the city — among the few buildings that came through the Great Fire of 1835 untouched, and, thanks to the New York Landmarks Conservancy, saved to become the Fraunces Tavern Block Historic District.","source_id":"f781f822-038c-4e67-b8e6-c574371be401","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"The darkest chapter, though, is the most recent one.","source_id":"f765ed0c-2fc7-4d3a-ba8c-6c05b9815c58","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"In 1975 the Armed Forces Puerto Rican National Liberation Front bombed Fraunces Tavern, killing four people and injuring dozens.","source_id":"f765ed0c-2fc7-4d3a-ba8c-6c05b9815c58","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2},{"text":"They chose it deliberately, for two reasons — as a symbol of American ideals, and because it's one of the few landmark buildings in New York with a Caribbean connection.","source_id":"f765ed0c-2fc7-4d3a-ba8c-6c05b9815c58","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":2}]}
